title: Multidimensional Error Attribution Explorer and Tracing Hook
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Add a new error-attribution surface that joins per-request tracing hooks with enriched error classification. The Explorer will let SREs and engineers slice failure rates and p99 latency by orthogonal dimensions (model_variant, sequence_length_bucket, route, backend_pool, region, batch_size). Instrumentation changes must attach compact error_class tags (timeout, overload, model_err, client_err, server_err, transport_err) and numeric reason codes (http_status / grpc_code) to spans and logs so downstream pipelines can group and index effectively.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks emit 'error_class' and 'error_reason' tags for all handled error flows (timeouts, overloaded queue drops, model runtime errors, HTTP/gRPC codes)
Log/metrics pipeline transforms attach the same error tags to request-level trace IDs and make them queryable in the Explorer within 2 minutes of ingestion
Explorer UI shows failure-rate and latency distributions across at least 6 dimensions (route, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, backend_pool, region, status_code) with filter and compare functionality
Runbook links appear for any slice exceeding configured thresholds and can be opened directly from the Explorer
No more than 12% incremental storage/ingest cost for enriched traces in our staging region during a 48-hour smoke test
notes: Motivation: current dashboards aggregate failure counts but cannot attribute spikes to model vs infra vs transport. This increases incident MTTR.
We need compact tags to limit cardinality: use buckets for seq_len (<=128,129-512,513-2048,>2048) and limit model_variant to canonical names only.
Prefer tagging at the host runtime boundary (inference proxy) to capture queue/drop and kernel-failure events, and in the http/grpc gateway to capture transport codes.
Pipeline: add a lightweight enrich stage to metrics/log-forwarder that joins traces by trace_id and materializes per-request docs into the Explorer index.
Retention/Cost: propose 30d of indexed Explorer docs and archive raw traces to object storage for 90d.
Telemetry gating: add flag 'observability.error_explorer.enabled' per-deployment for staged rollout.
SLO interaction: create automatic alerts when a slice's error_rate or p99 latency crosses defined SLO buckets; initial SLOs defined by PM team.
work_breakdown: Instrumentation: add error_class/error_reason tags at inference proxy (2 spikes)
Gateway: annotate HTTP/gRPC spans with transport status and client metadata (1 spike)
Pipeline: write enricher that joins traces->request docs and indexes into Explorer index (3 spikes)
UI: Explorer front-end work to support multi-dimension filters and runbook linking (3 spikes)
Runbook authoring: PM/ops draft initial runbooks for top 10 common slices (1 spike)
Rollout & smoke: staged enablement, 48-hour smoke, cost verification (1 spike)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Cardinality blowup if model_variant or route tags are too high—enforce canonicalization at tag source
Indexing cost: full request docs are heavier than metrics; tradeoff between queryability and cost. Start with narrow retention and expand if necessary
Sampling: we will initially ingest all error traces and 1% of successful traces for baseline. This may bias median latency views; callouts will show sample rate
Backpressure: adding enrich stage could add ~200ms to path if run synchronously—pipeline must be async and join by trace_id downstream
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): instrument inference proxy + gateway, enable enrich pipeline for staging, index 48h of data
Phase 2 (canary): enable in 10% of prod traffic, verify cost < 12% delta and query performance
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to 50% then 100% with monitoring for index size and query latency
Phase 4 (GA): update Console documentation and create default slice alerts for common SLOs
updates: 2026-03-03: Spike completed - prototype tags emitted from inference proxy; observed tag cardinality of model_variant reduced by canonicalization step
2026-03-07: Enricher PoC can join traces->requests at ~2000 req/s in staging; needs optimization for peak traffic
2026-03-11: UI mockups reviewed by PM and UX; agreed on compact multi-select filters and side-by-side compare
2026-03-12: Cost projection added to acceptance criteria; infra asked to provide 72-hour ingest estimate for all regions
